title: A Deadline for the Asset
premise: Ada Sterling, a fixer for the Meridian Group—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent two years burying the guilt of an extraction gone wrong in Lisbon. When a dead asset's voiceprint unlocks a hidden server in Tbilisi, Ada discovers the 'incident' was orchestrated from inside her own agency, and that the defector she's ordered to extract, cryptographer Lena Marsh, is bait designed to flush out everyone who knows the truth. As Ada and Lena run from Meridian's own hunters across three countries, duty curdles into love, and Ada must choose between the only belonging she's ever had and exposing the people who made her. In the end, Ada burns her cover to deliver the evidence to a journalist in Vienna, trades herself for Lena's freedom, and walks out of custody months later into a life with no handler and no debt—the first night she sleeps through.
about_author: Gideon Voss is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade drafting contracts for organizations he was never allowed to name. He writes thrillers about the paperwork of violence from a farmhouse in northern Portugal.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers No Phones
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A routine cleanup job in Vienna—a wiped laptop, a paid-off widow—establishes his competence and his insomnia; he hasn't slept a full night since Lisbon. Emotional beat: hollow professionalism masking grief.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. An encrypted archive pings him: a voiceprint sample of Tomas Reiner, the asset who died in Lisbon, unlocks a server in Tbilisi containing files labeled MERIDIAN-INTERNAL. Emotional beat: dread reawakening—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Handler's Mercy
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. His handler, Corvus, orders him to stand down and take mandatory leave, which Ada reads as containment. He copies the files anyway. Emotional beat: first crack in loyalty.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Lena's POV introduced. Cryptographer Lena Marsh walks into a Tbilisi safehouse offering Meridian's financial ledger in exchange for extraction, unaware—or pretending not to know—that her file is flagged BAIT-CONFIRMED. Emotional beat: wary courage.

chapters.title: Extraction Order
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Despite the flag, Ada volunteers for the extraction, telling himself it's about answers, not redemption. Corvus approves too easily. Emotional beat: self-deception dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Tbilisi, Four Minutes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pickup goes wrong on schedule: a second team arrives exactly when the files predicted. Ada realizes the ambush used his own tradecraft patterns. Emotional beat: betrayal becoming personal.

chapters.title: Running Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the run through Georgia's borderlands, Lena decrypts enough of the ledger to find payments routed through Lisbon the week of the incident. Emotional beat: her cynicism softening toward the man protecting her.

chapters.title: What Lisbon Cost
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback braided with present. We finally see the incident: Tomas died because someone fed his location to hostiles—and Ada pulled the trigger on the door that killed him. Emotional beat: guilt given a face.

chapters.title: Corvus Calls
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Corvus offers Ada a clean exit if he delivers Lena to a 'debriefing' in Istanbul. Ada hears the euphemism for what it is. Emotional beat: the choice sharpening.

chapters.title: Night Train to Batumi
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Packed into a freight compartment, Ada and Lena trade truths instead of sleep; something unguarded passes between them. Emotional beat: intimacy born of exhaustion and honesty.

chapters.title: The Second Flag
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena finds her own name in the ledger—not as defector but as contractor, hired by Meridian to build the very server that lured Ada. She hides it. Emotional beat: complicity and fear of losing him.

chapters.title: Istanbul Debrief
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada delivers a decoy—Lena is already on a ferry to Athens—to buy time, and confronts a Meridian deputy who all but confirms internal orchestration. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing loyalty.

chapters.title: Athens Safehouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Reunited, they plan to move the full ledger to a journalist in Vienna. Ada admits he knew what she was before he extracted her. Emotional beat: trust surviving deception—love against duty declared.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Plaka
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Meridian's cleaners find them; a brutal close-quarters escape costs Ada his left-hand mobility and nearly both their lives. Emotional beat: the price of the choice made flesh.

chapters.title: Corvus Unmasked
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Cross-referencing travel records, Lena proves Corvus authored the Lisbon leak—and the BAIT flag—to erase witnesses including Ada himself. Emotional beat: fury and heartbreak fused.

chapters.title: The Offer He Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Meridian captures Lena and offers Ada full reinstatement and absolution for Lisbon in exchange for walking away. For one long night he almost says yes. Emotional beat: the darkest hour—belonging weaponized against love.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With a 48-hour window before Lena is 'debriefed,' Ada goes off-grid entirely, burning every Meridian credential he has to reach her holding site outside Bratislava. Emotional beat: resolve without safety net.

chapters.title: Bratislava Break
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A desperate, improvised assault on the holding site—no backup, no cover—frees Lena but leaves them trapped in the sub-basement as alarms rise. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into commitment.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Confrontation with Corvus in the flooding lower level: Ada chooses exposure over execution, recording Corvus's confession as Lena triggers the ledger upload to Vienna. Corvus dies by his own contingency; Ada nearly follows. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid in blood.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In Vienna, the journalist publishes; governments scramble, Meridian dissolves into shell companies overnight. Lena testifies under protection while Ada vanishes into custody negotiations. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Terms of Release
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. After four months of debriefs, Ada trades silence for amnesty and walks free—stateless, unemployed, unowned. Emotional beat: freedom that feels like falling.

chapters.title: First Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing. Ada finds Lena at a coastal house in Portugal; no handlers, no deadlines, the sea doing the work of forgiveness. He sleeps through the night for the first time since Lisbon. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
